name: @healthier-business/hub-mcp

tools.name: hb_status
tools.description: Who am I and what may I do? Calls GET /auth/me and reports: environment (live or sandbox), base URL, key name and prefix, the key's scopes, whether writes are enabled, the toolsets, the approval state of each sensitive area (Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work need the Hub's one-off approval for live use; GET /account/api-access, any key), and the last-seen rate limit. Never reveals a key or token. Call this first.

tools.name: hb_search_operations
tools.description: Search the 213 Hub API v2 operations by text, toolset (portal), method or scope. Returns id, method, path, summary, scope, flags (credits, health data, destructive) and whether each is callable now. Start here, then hb_describe_operation, then hb_call_operation.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "book practical training", "candidate compliance", "webhook".

toolset.description: Portal: hub, account, online-training, occupational-health, references, practical-training, virtual-bls-training, clinical-interviews, registration-monitoring, dbs-rtw, clinical-appraisals, training-verification, authentication.

scope.description: Substring of the required scope, e.g. "bookings:write".

tools.name: hb_describe_operation
tools.description: Full detail of one operation: parameters, body schema with required fields and an example, required scope, side effects (credits, health data, destructive, idempotency), documented errors, and a ready example call for hb_call_operation. Read this before any write.

tools.name: hb_call_operation
tools.description: [LIVE Hub] Call any Hub API v2 operation by id. Validates against the spec before sending; adds an Idempotency-Key to writes; follows pagination with all_pages (capped). The server is READ-ONLY: only GET operations run; writes are refused. Put path parameters in path_params, filters in query, JSON in body. Use `fields` (dotted paths such as ["candidate_ref","name"]) to keep answers small. Credits are units; money is integer pence with a currency. Never ask the user for an API key in chat.

operation_id.description: Operation id from hb_search_operations, e.g. hub.candidates.list.

path_params.description: Values for {placeholders} in the path, e.g. {"candidate_ref":"<uuid>"}.

body.description: JSON request body (object). For file uploads use {"filename","content_base64","content_type"} for file fields.

headers.description: Only headers the operation declares (e.g. Idempotency-Key). Authorization is never settable.

confirm.description: Sandbox writes only: true to confirm. On the LIVE Hub this does nothing: use confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: LIVE writes: the one-time token from the plan the first call returned. Send it, with the same arguments, only after the user approved that plan. It works once, for those exact arguments, for ten minutes.

all_pages.description: List operations: fetch following pages and merge data.

max_pages.description: With all_pages: pages to fetch (default 5, max 20).

fields.description: Keep only these dotted paths of each record in `data`.

idempotency_key.description: Reuse the key from a plan or an earlier unknown-outcome write to repeat it safely.

tools.name: hb_list_events
tools.description: List the 73 webhook events Hub can send (type and one-line summary). Optionally filter by portal prefix (e.g. "occupational-health") or text. Knowledge only: sends nothing.

portal.description: Portal prefix, e.g. occupational-health, practical-training, hub.

query.description: Text to match in the event type or summary.

tools.name: hb_describe_event
tools.description: Describe one webhook event: summary, delivery behaviour (retries), the `data` payload schema and a sample payload. Payloads hold ids, statuses, dates and a candidate_ref, never names, emails or health data. Knowledge only.

tools.name: hb_verify_webhook_signature
tools.description: Pure local helper (no network): verify or compute a Hub webhook signature. The signature is "sha256=" plus the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "{timestamp}.{raw body}" with the endpoint secret; deliveries older or newer than 300 seconds are rejected. Pass the raw body byte-for-byte. The secret is read from HB_WEBHOOK_SECRET unless passed (prefer a sandbox secret if you pass it in chat). Omit `signature` to just compute it.

body.description: The raw request body exactly as received.

signature.description: The X-Hub-Signature header. Omit to compute the expected signature.

secret.description: Endpoint signing secret. Defaults to env HB_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

now_epoch_seconds.description: Override the current time (for testing recorded deliveries).

tools.name: hb_search_guides
tools.description: Search the bundled guides by words and get the best matches with a snippet and the resource to read (hb://guides/<name>). Covers the Hub API v2 developer guides and the developer portal guides (sign up, sandboxes, keys, webhooks, Playground, going to production). Knowledge only: sends nothing, needs no key.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "create sandbox", "rotate webhook secret", "idempotency key".

group.description: "api" = Hub API guides, "portal" = developer portal (console) guides. Default all.

tools.name: hb_find_candidate
tools.description: Find candidates by name, email, the client's own candidate reference, or a candidate_ref (uuid), in one call. Returns a compact table: candidate_ref, name, email, roles, compliance status, next expiry, and which portals have a record for the person. Uses hub.candidates.list (or .show for a uuid) plus hub.candidates.show for the first 5 matches. Read-only; needs hub:candidates:read. Say the result includes the operation ids called.

query.description: Name, email, own candidate reference, or candidate_ref uuid. Every word must match. Max 100 characters.

active_only.description: Only active candidates (default: inactive ones are listed too).

include_portals.description: Look up which portals have a record for each of the first 5 matches (default true).

tools.name: hb_candidate_overview
tools.description: One-call summary of a candidate across every portal the key can reach: online training, practical training, virtual BLS, references, DBS and right to work, registration monitoring, clinical appraisals, clinical interviews, certificate verifications (training verification, linked by candidate_ref) and occupational health. One line per record with status and dates. Checks the key's scopes first, calls only what is allowed, and says which portals were skipped and why. Occupational health is statuses and dates only (never answers, clearance detail or documents). Read-only. Needs hub:candidates:read plus the portal read scopes you want. Live use of Occupational Health needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate_ref uuid (find it with hb_find_candidate).

portals.description: Optional: only these portals (toolset names such as "practical-training"). Default all.

tools.name: hb_account_summary
tools.description: One compact answer about the account: the key (name, expiry, scopes), credit and balance figures for every portal the key can read, and the webhook endpoints with health (active, consecutive failures, last response) and the latest deliveries of up to 5 endpoints. Credits are units; money is shown as an amount in the currency. Read-only. Uses auth.me.show, each portal credits.show, webhooks.endpoints.list and webhooks.deliveries.list as the key allows. Webhook URLs are shown without query strings. Live use of Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

tools.name: hb_needs_attention
tools.description: What needs action right now, built only from what the API exposes and the key can read: failed or disabled webhook endpoints, unacknowledged DBS/RTW and registration alerts, bookings awaiting payment (practical, virtual BLS, clinical interviews, clinical appraisals), appraisals awaiting documents, expired or lapsing online training, expired reference requests, certificate verifications that failed or have been pending for over an hour (training verification), and occupational health counts (awaiting candidate, rejected or failed; counts only, no health detail). Read-only. Portals the key cannot read are listed as skipped. Live use of Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

tools.name: hb_go_live_check
tools.description: Read-only go-live readiness report: environment, key scopes against the portals you say you need (optional `portals`), wildcard and expiry warnings, sandbox-versus-live mismatches, webhook endpoints present and healthy, the IP allowlist (the API does not show it: says so), and the remaining manual steps from the going-live guide (hb://guides/going-live). Sends only reads. Live use of Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

portals.description: Portals (toolsets) the integration needs, for example ["hub","practical-training","account"]. Webhook management is "account".

tools.name: hb_training_progress
tools.description: Online training for one candidate in one call: the account summary, every course with status, grade, dates and certificate availability, the modules (counted by status per course), and the practical results. `course_id` adds the full result of one course; `available_courses` lists the courses the account can assign. Read-only. Uses online-training.candidates.show, .results, .results.show, .modules, .practical-results and online-training.courses.list.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate_ref uuid (find it with hb_find_candidate).

course_id.description: Show the full result of this course.

search.description: With available_courses: part of a course name.

tools.name: hb_list_bookings
tools.description: Bookings across practical training, virtual BLS, clinical interviews and clinical appraisals in one compact table (portal, id, candidate, what, start, status, payment). Filter by portals, candidate_ref, date range (clinical appraisals use the booking creation date) and status. Practical training no-shows are included unless include_no_shows is false. Read-only. No candidate contact details, NMC numbers, reports or links are returned.

status.description: Booking status, for example pending, booked, rescheduled, cancelled.

include_no_shows.description: Also list practical training no-shows (default true).

tools.name: hb_credits
tools.description: Credit and balance figures for every portal the key can reach (online training, occupational health, practical training, virtual BLS, clinical interviews, clinical appraisals, training verification), with the most recent transactions, plus the occupational health credit packages. Credits are units; money is shown as an amount with its currency. Read-only. Portals the key cannot read are listed as skipped. Live use of Occupational Health needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

tools.name: hb_webhook_health
tools.description: Webhook endpoint health: active flag, consecutive failures (Hub switches an endpoint off at 25), last response code, and the recent failed deliveries of each endpoint with a summary of the response codes. The API gives status, attempts and HTTP code but not error text (that is on the Developer page). URLs are shown without query strings. Read-only. Uses webhooks.endpoints.list/.show and webhooks.deliveries.list.

tools.name: hb_monitoring_alerts
tools.description: Alerts from DBS and right to work, registration monitoring and occupational health in one list. Filters: portals, acknowledged (true or false), severity, type, limit. `alert_id` with `portal` shows one DBS/RTW or registration alert in full. Occupational health alerts are statuses only (type, severity, status, date, candidate_ref): never names, reasons, clearance or documents. Read-only. Uses dbs-rtw.alerts.list/.show, registration-monitoring.alerts.list/.show and occupational-health.alerts.list. Live use of Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

acknowledged.description: DBS/RTW and registration alerts only: true for acknowledged, false for open.

tools.name: hb_worker_status
tools.description: Look up a DBS/right to work or registration monitoring worker (by worker_id, search text or candidate_ref) and show the current result, the latest verification history and the evidence metadata (type, date, size). Certificate numbers appear only in the masked form the API returns; date of birth, contact details, registration numbers and the evidence files themselves are never returned. Read-only. Uses {portal}.workers.show/.list/.verification/.evidence. Live use of DBS & Right To Work needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

search.description: Part of the name or email.

tools.name: hb_billing_summary
tools.description: Usage and bills for DBS and right to work and for registration monitoring: trial status, billing type, this month's estimate (active workers and amounts) and the latest bills with status and due date. Money is shown as an amount with its currency. Read-only. Uses {portal}.billing.usage and .billing.bills. Invoices (PDF) are not fetched. Live use of DBS & Right To Work needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

tools.name: hb_get_report
tools.description: Certificate and report details with how to download them: practical training, virtual BLS and online training certificates, clinical interview report, clinical appraisal evaluation report, the occupational health reports list, and for Training Verification the verification report (kind verification_report, available once verified) and the submitted certificate file (kind verification_certificate); booking_id is the verification id for those. Returns whether the file exists, its metadata and the exact API address and instructions to download it. File bytes are never returned in the answer: with check_download=true the server fetches the file only to report its type and size, then discards it. Interview and appraisal reports are health data, and verification certificates and reports are personal data: use only what the task needs. Read-only. Uses the booking show operations, the certificate/report download operations and occupational-health.reports.list. Live use of Occupational Health needs the Hub's one-off approval (in the Hub under Developer > API access; by default these areas; account.api-access.show or hb_status shows the state per area); until then live calls answer 403 api_access_*. The sandbox is always open.

booking_id.description: For booking based kinds (for verification_report and verification_certificate: the verification id).

certificate_type.description: Online training: current (default), assigned, all, excl-expired, incl-expired, range, course, care, cstf.

check_download.description: Fetch the file once to report its content type and size (bytes are discarded).

tools.name: hb_verification_status
tools.description: Follow certificate verifications. With verification_id: that verification in full (status, request type, the result with the courses found (for an Automated request only the courses the certificate names) and the reason code when not verified (an Automated request that cannot be matched always has the one reason `other`), the charge and whether it was refunded, the timeline of events, and whether the report and the certificate file are available). Without it: a list, newest first, filtered by status (pending, processing, verified, not_found, rejected, failed), request_type, candidate_ref, client_reference and created_from/created_to. Metadata only: the certificate file and the report are never fetched or returned (download them with the Hub API; the answer says how). Email addresses are left out. Read-only. Uses training-verification.verifications.list, .show and .events.

verification_id.description: Show one verification with its timeline.

candidate_ref.description: List filter: verifications linked to this candidate.

instructions:
NOT CONFIGURED: no HB_API_KEY is set, so Hub calls will fail. Do not ask for a key in chat. Tell the user to get one from the developer portal and walk them through it with hb://guides/portal-create-your-account (sign up with a work email and verify it) and hb://guides/portal-sandboxes (create a sandbox), then hb://guides/portal-api-keys-and-tokens (create a test key); the get-started-in-sandbox prompt does this step by step. They put the key in HB_API_KEY and the sandbox address in HB_BASE_URL in the MCP server config, then restart.

No sandbox base URL (HB_BASE_URL) is set, so this server points at the default LIVE Hub. Someone building or learning should use a sandbox: hb://guides/portal-sandboxes shows how to create one and where its base address is.

Healthier Business Hub API v2 (213 operations). Environment: LIVE (real people, real data, real credits). The server is read-only: only GET operations run. Writes are refused until the owner sets HB_READ_ONLY=false (and, for live, HB_ALLOW_LIVE_WRITES=true).

Task tools do the common jobs in one call with sensible defaults, through the same safety pipeline as hb_call_operation (read-only default, plan-then-confirm, idempotency, secret redaction); prefer them when they match, and each result lists the operation ids it called. Every task tool that writes is two calls: the first returns the options or plan and sends nothing, the second needs the confirmation_token from the first call (in a sandbox confirm=true also works) after the user agrees; they are hidden while the server is read-only. Which tool for which job: hb_find_candidate (find a person by name, email or reference); hb_candidate_overview (one line per record across the portals the key can reach; health data only as statuses and dates); hb_training_progress (a candidate's online training); hb_list_bookings (bookings across the booking portals); hb_credits (credit balances and recent transactions); hb_account_summary (key, credits and webhook health in one answer); hb_needs_attention (what needs action now); hb_monitoring_alerts (DBS/RTW, registration and occupational health alerts); hb_worker_status (a monitored worker and the latest check); hb_billing_summary (monitoring usage and bills); hb_get_report (certificate and report details and how to download them); hb_webhook_health (failing webhook endpoints and deliveries); hb_go_live_check (readiness report before going live); hb_verification_status (follow certificate verifications: status, result, timeline, report and certificate availability). Use the generic tools for everything else. HB_TASK_TOOLS (all, core or none) chooses which task tools are offered.

Workflow: hb_status first; then hb_search_operations to find an operation, hb_describe_operation to read its exact shape, hb_call_operation to run it. hb_list_events / hb_describe_event explain the 73 webhook events; hb_verify_webhook_signature checks a delivery locally.

People are addressed only by candidate_ref (a uuid); never by internal id, and never invent one: list or search candidates first. A candidate reference of the client's own (candidate_reference) is different from candidate_ref.

Scopes: each operation needs a scope like occupational-health:requests:read (a :write scope also grants :read). 403 insufficient_scope means the key lacks it; tell the user which scope to add. Do not try other endpoints to work around it.

Sensitive areas: for a LIVE key, Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work (by default; staff choose) need the Hub's one-off approval of the organisation, under Developer > API access in the Hub. hb_status shows the state per area (account.api-access.show is the same call). A 403 api_access_not_approved, api_access_pending, api_access_rejected or api_access_revoked (or webhook_events_not_approved on a webhook endpoint) is not retryable: tell the user plainly which area and state and that they ask for approval in the Hub; do not try other endpoints to work around it. The sandbox is always open.

Lists are paginated (page, per_page up to 100, default 25). Prefer filters and the `fields` argument to keep answers small; use all_pages only when you need everything.

Money is integer pence with a currency; credits are units, not money. Some operations use credits or balance: say so before running them.

Responses marked health_data contain special-category health information: use only what the task needs and do not repeat it elsewhere.

Secrets: the API key lives only in the server environment (HB_API_KEY). Never ask the user to paste a key, token or webhook secret in chat, and never print one.

Sandbox first: build and test in a sandbox, go live only after the user asks (see the go-live-checklist prompt). Quote request_id when reporting an error.

Docs are available as resources: hb://guides/<name> (authentication, errors, scopes-and-permissions, ...), hb://portals/<toolset>, hb://spec/operations/<id>, hb://spec/events/<type>. hb_search_guides finds the right guide by words.

The developer portal (where a developer signs up, makes sandboxes, test keys and webhooks, uses the API Playground and request log, books support and goes to production) has its own guides: hb://guides/portal-overview, portal-create-your-account, portal-sandboxes, portal-api-keys-and-tokens, portal-webhooks, portal-simulate, portal-api-playground, portal-request-log-and-debugging, portal-support-and-booking-a-call, portal-go-to-production, and more. Use them when the user asks how to do something in the portal, not only about the API.
